citation: Yuvaraj, Rajamanickam, N. P. Guhan Seshadri, Sampathraman Samyuktha, Jack S. Fogarty, Jun Song Huang, Samuel Tan, and Teck Kiong Wong. "EEG-Based Functional Connectivity Patterns During Boredom in an Educational Context." Scientific Reports 15 (2025): 35439. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-19245-7.
discipline: cognitive neuroscience / educational psychology; empirical EEG functional-connectivity study of boredom in an educational context
thesis: Using spectral-coherence-based EEG functional-connectivity matrices (five bands, five graph-theoretic network measures) recorded from 64-channel scalp EEG while 73 university students watched an educational boredom-inducing lecture video versus a comparison 'excitement' video, the authors show boredom is characterized by significantly higher global efficiency and lower characteristic path length in the alpha, beta, and gamma bands, and higher gamma-band clustering coefficient and local efficiency, relative to the comparison condition. They interpret this as evidence that boredom involves active, locally-integrated yet globally-efficient network reorganization reflecting increased internal processing, not passive disengagement, and argue this challenges the view that boredom only hinders learning.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.summary: States hypothesis, method, and headline result (higher global efficiency and lower characteristic path length in alpha/beta/gamma bands during boredom, relative to excitement).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Defines boredom; surveys its educational costs (Westgate & Wilson; Eastwood et al.; Pekrun et al.; Mann & Robinson; meta-analytic evidence); motivates EEG for affective/cognitive research; reviews prior EEG functional-connectivity work on emotion and mind-wandering (DMN literature; discrete-emotion coherence studies); states aim and hypothesis.

sections.title: Materials
sections.summary: Participants (N=84, NTU students); Ethical statement (NTU IRB-2022-1048); Boredom stimulus and experiment protocol (excitement video + boring lecture video; State Affect Questionnaire); Scalp EEG recordings (64-channel AntNeuro system); Procedure (SoLEC lab session, ~60 min).

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary: EEG data annotation (SAQ-based labeling; 84->73 exclusion); EEG signal preprocessing (downsampling, wavelet denoising, band decomposition); Coherence and construction of EEG functional-connectivity matrices (61x61 per band per epoch); EEG functional-connectivity network analysis (Ceff, Cpl, Eglo, Eloc, Nstr formulas; Brain Connectivity Toolbox); Statistical analysis (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Bonferroni correction).

sections.title: Results
sections.summary: Boredom functional connectivity: SAQ manipulation check; band-by-band connectivity maps (delta through gamma); node-strength topography (z-value comparison). Network measures in excitement and boredom stimulus: Ceff/Cpl/Eglo/Eloc compared by band via split violin plots.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.summary: Interprets gamma-band findings as reflecting internally-directed attention/mind-wandering and cortical effort to sustain engagement; discusses smaller theta/alpha/beta effects; interprets node-strength topography; reframes boredom's role in learning as potentially catalytic rather than purely detrimental.

sections.title: Limitations and future work
sections.summary: Single lab-based elicitation stimulus; no analysis of viewing-duration/SAQ correlation; only four graph measures examined; spectral coherence's susceptibility to volume-conduction artifacts; recommends imaginary coherence and directed-connectivity methods (DTF, partial directed coherence, Granger causality) for future work.

sections.title: Study implications
sections.summary: Implications for educational design (identifying under/overactive brain regions to tailor instruction), personalized interventions (gamification, adaptive learning technologies), and broader cognitive processes (creativity, decision-making).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: Restates that boredom is associated with distinct gamma/beta/alpha connectivity changes; argues boredom may activate brain processes that improve connectivity and thinking efficiency, challenging the view that boredom only impedes learning.

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: explicitly operationalized as induced, transient state boredom via a single validated video; trait scales (Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, Boredom Proneness Scale) named and set aside as unsuited to this transient, single-exposure design

constructs.label: boredom proneness
constructs.treatment: named only as an individual antecedent-susceptibility factor in the introduction's causal framing, and via the (uncited-in-use) Boredom Proneness Scale; not independently measured

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: gamma/beta connectivity increases during boredom interpreted, via prior mind-wandering/Default Mode Network literature, as reflecting a shift toward internally directed attention or mind-wandering

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: boredom framed as disengagement from the external environment with a hypothesized distinct neural signature, contrasted with ordinary resting-state DMN dominance during mind-wandering

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: reframed in Discussion/Conclusion as a state that may prompt the brain to seek new sources of stimulation rather than signal mere deficit; closes on boredom as a potential catalyst for cognitive growth

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: operationalized directly as the study's 'excitement' comparison-video condition; flow-theory-adjacent engagement literature (Shernoff et al., 2003) cited in the introduction to frame boredom's opposite pole

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: boredom-inducing stimulus explicitly engineered around monotony: piloted lecture video selected for slow, monotonous delivery and low-value content with minimal cognitive challenge

measures.label: EEG functional connectivity
measures.signal: spectral coherence (Cxy) between all pairs of 61 EEG channels (mastoids and EOG excluded), computed per 2-second epoch across five decomposed frequency bands (delta 0-4Hz, theta 4-8Hz, alpha 8-16Hz, beta 16-32Hz, gamma 32-64Hz); coherence in [0,1], retained as a full unthresholded 61x61 weighted matrix (thresholded at 0.6 only for display)
measures.apparatus: AntNeuro eegoTM sports amplifier, 64-channel gel electrode cap (10-10 system), 1000 Hz sampling down-sampled to 256 Hz, CPz active reference, AFz ground; wavelet-packet band decomposition (Daubechies db9, level 6); five graph-theoretic network measures (Ceff, Cpl, Eglo, Eloc, Nstr) computed via the Brain Connectivity Toolbox in MATLAB 2023b; visualized with BrainNet Viewer
measures.sample_n: N=84 recruited (38M/46F, mean age 26.90+/-5.29); N=73 retained after excluding 11 participants whose SAQ responses did not confirm the intended emotional state per video
measures.key_result: Gamma band showed the largest, most consistent differences across all four global/local measures: higher Ceff (z=-14.79, p<.001) and Eloc (z=-21.94, p<.001), lower Cpl (z=-25.36, p<.001), higher Eglo (z=-24.17, p<.001) during boredom vs. excitement; alpha and beta showed smaller but significant Cpl/Eglo differences (and alpha Eloc); delta showed no significant differences (FAITHFUL-Yuvaraj et al., p.10)

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.signal: 5-item State Affect Questionnaire (SAQ), adapted from PANAS, rating excitement/disgust/neutral/boredom/distress intensity 0(none)-8(extreme), completed within a 90-second inter-stimulus window after each video
measures.apparatus: paper-based questionnaire (Appendix 1), administered immediately post-video; used both as the EEG emotion-labeling ground truth and, via two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (video type x emotion), as the study's manipulation check
measures.sample_n: N=84 completed; N=73 retained after exclusion
measures.key_result: Boredom-video 'boredom' ratings (mean 5.29+/-2.67) were significantly higher than all other emotions on that video (p<.001); excitement video predominantly elicited excitement (2.98+/-2.77) and neutral (2.20+/-2.54) ratings, confirming successful, differentiated induction of both target states (FAITHFUL-Yuvaraj et al., p.9)

measures.label: heart rate / HRV; gaze variance / fixation dispersion (collected, not analyzed)
measures.signal: electrocardiogram and eye-gaze data recorded continuously and synchronized with EEG via Chronos hardware event markers, alongside galvanic skin response collected separately at 128 Hz via Shimmer
measures.apparatus: same session/apparatus as the EEG recording; multimodal signals were time-locked to video onset/offset but excluded from this paper's analysis pipeline
measures.key_result: Not analyzed: 'For this study, only EEG data were obtained and analyzed' -- a caveat for any future comparison to a multimodal VR Attention Study dataset channel, since this paper demonstrates EEG-only analysis despite multimodal collection (FAITHFUL-Yuvaraj et al., p.5)

measures.label: EEG eyes-open vs. eyes-closed (not used as a resting baseline)
measures.signal: not applicable -- no resting-state recording of any kind was collected
measures.key_result: Not treated: both experimental conditions are active, eyes-open video-viewing states differing only in induced affect; contrast with bor-sec-27 (Barry et al.), whose eyes-closed/eyes-open resting paradigm and non-equivalent-baseline finding this study's design implicitly sidesteps rather than addresses

readings.claim: This is presented as the first study to examine differences in functional brain networks during boredom, relative to a comparison state, in healthy adults using EEG.

SAQ ratings confirm successful, differentiated induction of both target states: boredom-video 'boredom' ratings were significantly higher than all other reported emotions (p<.001), while the 'excitement' video predominantly elicited excitement and neutral ratings.

Gamma-band coherence shows the largest, most consistent network-measure differences: higher clustering coefficient and local efficiency, lower characteristic path length, higher global efficiency during boredom versus excitement.

Alpha and beta bands show smaller but significant differences in characteristic path length and global efficiency (shorter/higher during boredom); delta shows no significant differences on any measure.

Node-strength topography shows the largest boredom-vs-excitement differences in gamma (broadly distributed) and beta (frontal/central), interpreted as a compensatory, effortful attempt to sustain cognitive engagement under low external stimulation.

The joint gamma-band pattern (higher clustering/efficiency, shorter path length) reflects more locally integrated yet globally less efficient network organization, consistent with elevated gamma during low-attention/disengaged states reported elsewhere.

Boredom is not a passive or idle state but one that engages active cognitive mechanisms; the observed connectivity/efficiency increases suggest functional reorganization compensating for reduced external input.

Brief episodes of boredom may trigger cognitive reorganization enabling deeper re-engagement with material, so boredom could act as a potential catalyst for cognitive growth rather than purely a barrier to learning.

The findings challenge the common belief that boredom only impedes learning, since increased gamma/beta activity during boredom may help the brain use its resources better in ways that can support learning.

Spectral coherence may include spurious zero-lag correlations due to volume conduction; future work should incorporate imaginary coherence or directed-connectivity methods (Directed Transfer Function, partial directed coherence, Granger causality) to refine and validate the findings.

tensions.axis: boredom as passive deficit/idling state vs. boredom as active, network-reorganizing functional state
tensions.note: the paper's central argumentative axis: gamma/beta connectivity increases and shortened path length are read as evidence against a purely passive-idling account, aligning with functional/regulatory theories of boredom (Bench & Lench; Elpidorou) over a purely deficit-oriented educational-psychology default.

tensions.axis: boredom as purely detrimental to learning vs. boredom as potentially catalytic for cognitive reorganization
tensions.note: the Conclusion explicitly stages this tension, arguing the traditional 'boredom only hinders learning' view should be revised in light of the observed gamma/beta connectivity increases.

tensions.axis: stimulus validated as 'neutral' in prior literature vs. this sample's actual affective response to it
tensions.note: the BBC 'Planet Earth' video, previously validated as neutral (Merrifield & Danckert, 2014), instead elicited significant self-reported excitement in this sample, forcing a post hoc relabeling of the comparison condition.

tensions.axis: coherence-based (undirected) functional connectivity vs. directed/causal connectivity measures (DTF, partial directed coherence, Granger causality)
tensions.note: acknowledged as a limitation: coherence cannot establish directionality or rule out volume-conduction artifacts; the authors recommend directed methods for future validation.

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study): EEG functional connectivity channel
dataset_channels.note: This paper's core measure -- EEG functional connectivity via spectral coherence across five bands and five Brain Connectivity Toolbox graph measures -- is an exact name-and-method match to the plausible future 'EEG functional connectivity' channel of the not-yet-built VR Attention Study dataset entry; the dataset entry does not exist on disk, so the specific measures/parameters it would use cannot be confirmed to match this paper's choices (P/anticipatory-application).
